citation: Somers, M.-A., Corrin, W., Sepanik, S., Salinger, T., Levin, J., & Zmach, C. (2010). The Enhanced Reading Opportunities Study Final Report: The Impact of Supplemental Literacy Courses for Struggling Ninth-Grade Readers (NCEE 2010-4021). Washington, DC: National Center for Education Evaluation and Regional Assistance, Institute of Education Sciences, U.S. Department of Education.
design: RCT; student-level random assignment to ERO vs non-ERO (business-as-usual) within high schools; schools randomly assigned to one of two supplemental literacy programs (RAAL vs Xtreme Reading); 34 high schools across 10 districts, 2 cohorts; subject = Reading; grade 9 (struggling ninth-grade readers).
problems: The report's 'effect size' is a standardized mean difference (impact/SD of non-ERO group) but does NOT report the standardizing SD as an exact figure; back-solving impact/ES gives SD ~9.3-9.8 depending on which rounded row is used. To avoid rounding loss I used the directly reported effect size and its SE from Appendix Table F.1 (2-dp). Sensitivity to SD choice shifts g by <=0.009, negligible. Per-arm n_t/n_c are GRADE respondent-sample sizes from Table 3.4 (totals match Table F.1 analysis Ns of 2,255 RAAL and 2,329 Xtreme).

effect_sizes.test_name: GRADE (Group Reading Assessment and Diagnostic Evaluation) reading comprehension subtest
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of program year / spring of ninth grade, both cohorts combined)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported standardized impact (effect size = impact / SD of non-ERO group in program year, all schools) taken directly from Appendix Table F.1 (ES = 0.12, ES SE = 0.04). Hedges' g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2253, J = 0.99967; g = 0.99967*0.12 = 0.11996; g_se = J*0.04 = 0.03999; g_var = g_se^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Appendix Table F.1 (p. F-5); cross-ref Table 3.4 (p. 66) and Table ES.2 discussion (p. ES-16)
effect_sizes.notes: RAAL = the more intensive of the two programs (Three TPD principles per registry row 111). Impact 1.23 standard score points, statistically significant (p=0.002). Mean_t is unadjusted ERO-group mean; mean_c is regression-adjusted non-ERO mean (Table 3.4); SDs not reported. Model: OLS regression-adjusted for school/cohort blocking + GRADE pretest + overage status (+ district reading/math tests + outcome pretest for high-school outcomes), Huber-White robust SE. Student-level random assignment within schools, so no cluster adjustment needed (cluster_adjusted=false; n_clusters/icc not applicable to the student-level contrast). Vocabulary subtest impact was ~0 (ES=0.00) and not extracted (separate test, not the primary reading comprehension outcome).

effect_sizes.test_name: GRADE (Group Reading Assessment and Diagnostic Evaluation) reading comprehension subtest
effect_sizes.timepoint: post (end of program year / spring of ninth grade, both cohorts combined)
effect_sizes.g_method: Reported standardized impact (effect size = impact / SD of non-ERO group in program year, all schools) taken directly from Appendix Table F.1 (ES = 0.05, ES SE = 0.04). Hedges' g = J*d with J = 1 - 3/(4*df-1), df = n_t+n_c-2 = 2327, J = 0.99968; g = 0.99968*0.05 = 0.04998; g_se = J*0.04 = 0.03999; g_var = g_se^2.
effect_sizes.page_ref: Appendix Table F.1 (p. F-5); cross-ref Table 3.4 (p. 66) and Table ES.2 discussion (p. ES-16)
effect_sizes.notes: Xtreme Reading = the less intensive of the two programs (One TPD principle per registry row 112). Impact 0.56 standard score points, NOT statistically significant (p=0.165). Mean_t is unadjusted ERO-group mean; mean_c is regression-adjusted non-ERO mean (Table 3.4); SDs not reported. Same OLS model and student-level random-assignment design as RAAL arm. The difference between the RAAL and Xtreme impacts is itself not statistically significant. Vocabulary subtest impact ES=0.03, not significant, not extracted.
